newsitem.title: USA: Canadian spot natgas prices extend gains in West.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot natgas prices extend gains in West.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices in the West continued to strengthen Thursday amid brisk storage injections and colder weather, market sources said.

At the AECO storage hub, prices rose an average of seven cents to about C$1.80 per gigajoule (GJ) as cold, snowy weather drained supplies and buyers tried to replenish lower-than-normal storage inventories.
Summer AECO prices were talked around C$1.67 per GJ.
In response to the firmer domestic market, prices at Sumas, Wash., also gained about seven cents to $1.48-1.50 per million British thermal units (mmBtu).
Cooler weather and diminished storage supplies were also cited as reasons for the price uptick at Sumas.
In the East, where storage inventories were ample, Niagara prices eased two cents to about $2.08-2.09 per mmBtu.
